**PM triage** — seat `session_01LZbWd2jNV1FErXTPSS4Dry` (PM seat #6367, `domain:engine` lane). Graded `bug` / `finding` / `priority:p2` / `pm:queue` / `domain:engine`. Routed to this lane because the relationship-key family is where it lives, ⚠️ though the three readers span `lint`, `plugin-security` and `verify` — see the split below.

The sharpest sentence in this card is the one about `data-model-rules.ts:167`: **the one component whose job is to tell an author their metadata is wrong is the component that accepts the wrong spelling.** A lint rule tolerating a key the spec refuses is not breadth, it is the gate reporting green on the thing it exists to catch.

### ⛔ Not dispatchable as one unit, and the card is right about why

The three readers have **different populations**, so a single "narrow them all" dispatch would be a guess dressed as consistency:

| reader | population | can the alias actually appear? |
|---|---|---|
| `lint/src/data-model-rules.ts:167` | authored source | **No** — `FieldSchema` refuses it upstream. Tolerance here is pure defect. |
| `verify/src/derive.ts:103` | possibly raw registered metadata | **Maybe** — `registerObject` deliberately skips Zod (#3896) |
| `plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:5846` | possibly raw registered metadata | **Maybe** — same route |

So the lint reader is a clean narrowing with a settled precedent (`validate-security-posture.ts:208` was narrowed to canonical-only **on purpose**, with the reason recorded in-file). The other two need someone to measure whether raw-`registerObject` metadata carrying `reference_to` actually reaches them, ⚠️ because narrowing a reader that legitimately sees legacy stored data would turn a tolerated read into a silent miss — the inverse defect.

Whoever takes this should expect to deliver the lint narrowing plus a **measurement** for the other two, and report rather than narrow if the measurement says the alias is reachable.

### Bearing on #13222

⚠️ Worth reading alongside #13222, which is now at `needs-user-decision`. This card is the same "one key, one answer" gap at three more doors, and it strengthens the general case without settling #13222's specific question — #13222's blast radius comes from the **published README** having taught the key to external users, which none of these three readers share.

⛔ Do not fold this into #13222 or vice versa.

Scope per PM triage: (1) narrow the lint reader `packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts:167` to canonical `reference` only, matching the recorded precedent in `validate-security-posture.ts:208`; (2) **measure** — not narrow — whether raw `registerObject` metadata carrying the rejected alias can actually reach `packages/verify/src/derive.ts:103` and `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:5846`. If the measurement shows the alias is reachable at either, that reader stays tolerant and the evidence is reported.

Staying out of `packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/**` entirely (#13222 is at needs-user-decision; PRs #13224 and #13238 are in flight there).

## PM triage update — one door closed, two measured REACHABLE, and I had the risk backwards

PR [#13322](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/13322) (`Part of`, not `Fixes` — this card stays open) narrows **one** of the three readers: `refOf` in `packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts`. Reviewed and accepted; held in draft until CI is complete and green.

The dispatch carried a stop condition, verbatim: *"⛔ If your measurement shows the alias IS reachable at either, do NOT narrow it. Report the finding with the evidence. That is a successful outcome for this dispatch, not a failure."* **It fired at both remaining readers.** Neither was touched. Below is what came back, with the parts I verified myself at the PR head rather than accepting on report.

### ⚠️ Correcting my own triage on this card

When I triaged #13250 I wrote that narrowing a reachable reader *"would turn a tolerated read into a **silent miss** — the inverse defect."* **That is wrong for reader A**, and wrong in the more dangerous direction. I checked the two lines myself at `03c514700`:

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:5959` — `if (!rel) return { ...RLS_DENY_FILTER };`
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:6152` — `if (!rel) throw new MasterDetailRelationMissingError(object, operation);`

`resolveCbpRelation` returning null is **fail-closed**. Narrowing that reader on a population that carries the alias does not produce a quiet wrong answer — it produces **zero rows for every non-admin caller on read and a throw on every write**. An availability outage, not a missed lint. Anyone weighing this decision against my earlier framing should weigh it against this one instead.

### Reader A — `plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:5846` — REACHABLE

Its population is `this.ql.getSchema(object)` → `SchemaRegistry.getObject`. Measured through the real registry: a `registerObject` → `getObject` round-trip preserves the field keys verbatim as `["type","label","reference_to","required"]`, and the reader expression `f?.reference ?? f?.reference_to ?? f?.referenceTo` resolves `"p_obj"` — with the canonical spelling resolving `"p_obj"` too as the positive control, so the alias result is not an artefact of a broken fixture.

The repo says the same thing in its own words at `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:1057-1058`: the registry is *"the one choke point EVERY door goes through … **including the doors that skip Zod and lint entirely**"* — and it names **#3896** and cloud's `rowColor.mapping` as **shipped** instances. The population is not hypothetical.

**Question 1:** narrow it, or keep the tolerance and make it loud?

- **A.** Keep the tolerant read; add an in-file note recording why it is deliberate (the `validate-security-posture.ts` precedent shape, inverted), plus a one-shot diagnostic when the alias is what resolved the relation. The author hears about it; no live deployment loses access.
- **B.** Narrow for one-key-one-answer consistency, accepting `RLS_DENY_FILTER` / `MasterDetailRelationMissingError` on any raw-registered `controlled_by_parent` object spelled with the alias.
- **C.** Narrow, but only behind a migration: sweep stored/raw metadata for the alias first, then flip.

The dev recommends **A**, and I agree with the reasoning: the defect this card is about — a tolerant consumer hiding an authoring mistake — is fully answered by making the tolerance **loud**, and the security reader is the wrong place to enforce spelling because its failure mode is denial rather than a message. **C is the only honest route to B**, and it is a separate card, not a rider on this one.

### Reader B — `verify/src/derive.ts:103` — REACHABLE

`loadConfig()` does not parse — it `bundleRequire`s the module and returns `mod.default`; parsing happens only if the authored module itself calls a `define*` helper. Measured three ways, each against a canonical positive control that produced an identical `relationalRefs` row: through `defineStack(cfg, { strict: false })` (a documented public option), through a plain-object config, and through the **real** `loadConfig()` on a real `objectstack.config.ts`. `deriveCrudCases()` read the alias into a `relationalRef` in all three. The strict door does refuse, correctly and loudly — it is simply not the only door.

**Question 2:** narrow it?

- **A.** Keep the tolerant read as-is.
- **B.** Narrow: an alias-spelled required relation becomes `blocked: 'required lookup field "parent" has no \`reference\` target'`.
- **C.** Narrow **and** report it as a distinct verify finding, so the run says *"this app spells a rejected alias"* rather than *"this object could not be derived."*

Recommendation **C**. Unlike reader A, derive's failure mode is a report line, not a denial — narrowing here costs coverage, not availability, so the honest direction is actually available. But a verifier that silently under-verifies is the exact defect **#5262** was about, so this is only safe if it reports the **reason**; **B alone would trade one silent gap for another.**

### Card state

Staying open and `pm:dispatched` while #13322 is in flight. When it lands I move this card to `needs-user-decision` — the two questions above are dispositions, not defects, and ⛔ no seat should proxy-decide them. In particular, reader A is a security-surface availability call and I am not going to make it on a maintainer's behalf.

## PR #13322 landed. Card → `needs-user-decision`: one door closed, two measured REACHABLE and left alone.

`pm:dispatched` → `needs-user-decision` (`get_labels` read first; `bug` / `priority:p2` / `domain:engine` untouched).

Verified by content on `origin/main`, ⛔ not by the `merged` boolean:

| reading | result |
|:--|--:|
| canonical-only guard `typeof r === 'string' && r ? r : undefined` | **1** |
| the old alias chain `def?.reference \|\| def?.reference_to` | **0** |
| the bound `const nonStringReference` fixture (the CI fix) | **1** |
| **control** — `refOf` present in the file | **4** |

### What is decided, and what is not

**Decided and shipped:** `refOf` in `packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts` reads only the canonical `reference`. That was the one clean narrowing — `@objectstack/lint` runs over a schema-parsed stack, so the alias could not legitimately reach it, and the tolerance made `relationship/missing-reference` — the rule whose whole job is to catch a relationship with no target — report a valid target for a field that has none.

**⛔ Not decided, and not for a seat to decide:** the two remaining readers. The dispatch's stop condition fired at both, and neither was touched.

### The two questions, restated for the maintainer

**Q1 — `plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts:5846`.** The alias IS reachable (`registerObject` skips Zod by design, #3896; the registry's own comment names those doors and cites two shipped instances). Options: **A** keep the tolerant read and make it *loud*; **B** narrow to canonical-only; **C** narrow behind a migration that sweeps stored/raw metadata first.

⚠️ **The consequence of B is the thing to weigh, and I had it backwards when I triaged this card.** I originally wrote that narrowing a reachable reader would produce *"a **silent miss** — the inverse defect."* It would not. Verified at the head:

- `:5959` — `if (!rel) return { ...RLS_DENY_FILTER };` → **0 rows for every non-admin caller**
- `:6152` — `if (!rel) throw new MasterDetailRelationMissingError(object, operation);`

`resolveCbpRelation` returning null is **fail-closed**. A raw-registered `controlled_by_parent` object spelled with the alias would go from "access derived from its master" to **everything denied, writes throw** — an availability outage on a population that provably exists, not a quiet wrong answer. Recommendation **A**; **C** is the only honest route to **B** and is a separate card.
